title: Product Manager (technical roles)
summary: Product managers decide what a team builds and why: they understand users, set priorities and work with engineers and designers to ship. It suits students from any branch who enjoy problem-solving, writing and talking to people, and who learn enough tech to earn engineers' trust.

sources.title: Product Manager: Role & Best Practices – Atlassian

nodes.title: Understand what a product manager does
nodes.summary: A PM owns the 'what' and 'why' of a product: customer insight, strategy and roadmap, priorities, team alignment and measuring results. Learn how this differs from a project manager, who focuses on 'how' and 'when'.

resources.title: Product Manager: Role & Best Practices – Atlassian
Product manager vs. project manager – Atlassian
Product Manager Roadmap – roadmap.sh

nodes.proof: Write a one-page note on an app you use: its users, the problem it solves and one feature you would change.

sources.title: Product Manager: Role & Best Practices – Atlassian

nodes.title: Technical foundations: how software and the web work
nodes.summary: Technical PMs must follow engineering discussions. Learn programming basics, how the internet and HTTP work, and what APIs are. Non-CS branches (ECE, EEE, MECH) should spend extra time here.

resources.title: CS50x: Introduction to Computer Science – Harvard
How does the Internet work? – MDN
Overview of HTTP – MDN

nodes.proof: Finish CS50x problem sets up to Python and explain in a short write-up what happens when you open a website.

sources.title: CS50x: Introduction to Computer Science – Harvard

nodes.title: Customer discovery and user interviews
nodes.summary: Good PMs start from real problems, not ideas. Learn to run user interviews and stakeholder interviews, ask open questions and dig for pain points, motivations and current workarounds.

resources.title: User Interviews 101 – NN/G
Stakeholder Interviews 101 – NN/G

nodes.proof: Interview 5 people about one problem and write a summary of the top 3 pain points with quotes.

nodes.title: Writing PRDs, user stories and acceptance criteria
nodes.summary: A product requirements document (PRD) states goals, assumptions, user stories, design and what is out of scope. User stories describe work from the user's view; acceptance criteria say when a story is done.

resources.title: What is a Product Requirements Document (PRD)? – Atlassian
User Stories with Examples and a Template – Atlassian
What is Acceptance Criteria? – Atlassian

nodes.proof: Write a 2-page PRD for one feature, with 5 user stories and acceptance criteria for each.

sources.title: What is a Product Requirements Document (PRD)? – Atlassian

nodes.title: Agile and Scrum: how teams ship
nodes.summary: Most software teams work in short cycles. Read the official Scrum Guide and learn backlogs, sprints and epics so you can plan work with engineers instead of handing over a long spec.

resources.title: The Scrum Guide – ScrumGuides.org
What is Scrum? – Atlassian
Product backlog: tips for creation and prioritization – Atlassian

nodes.proof: Turn your PRD into a prioritised backlog and plan a 2-week sprint with a clear sprint goal.

nodes.title: Prioritisation and roadmaps
nodes.summary: PMs always have more ideas than time. Learn frameworks such as RICE, MoSCoW and value vs. effort, and how to explain trade-offs and keep a roadmap that changes as you learn.

resources.title: Prioritization frameworks – Atlassian
Prioritizing ideas – Jira Product Discovery handbook

nodes.proof: Score 10 feature ideas with RICE, pick the top 3 and write one paragraph defending each choice.

nodes.title: Metrics, OKRs and basic SQL
nodes.summary: PMs check whether a change worked. Learn to set outcome-based goals (OKRs), pick metrics, and pull data yourself with SQL. Basic web analytics helps you read usage data.

resources.title: Intro to SQL: Querying and managing data – Khan Academy
OKRs: The Ultimate Guide – Atlassian
[GA4] Analytics Academy – Google Analytics Help

nodes.proof: Define one objective with 3 key results for a feature and write 3 SQL queries that would measure them.

sources.title: Outcomes vs Outputs – Jira Product Discovery handbook
Intro to SQL: Querying and managing data – Khan Academy

nodes.title: UX basics for PMs
nodes.summary: You will work closely with designers. Learn the 10 usability heuristics and how to run a quick usability test, so you can give useful feedback and check designs with real users.

resources.title: 10 Usability Heuristics for User Interface Design – NN/G
Usability (User) Testing 101 – NN/G

nodes.proof: Run a usability test of an existing app with 3–5 people and list the problems you found, ranked.

nodes.title: Ship a small product with a team
nodes.summary: Team up with 1–2 developer friends and take one real problem from interviews to a working launch. Owning a shipped product with real users and numbers is stronger evidence than any certificate.

resources.title: Free Product Requirements Document template – Atlassian
CS50's Web Programming with Python and JavaScript – Harvard

nodes.proof: A public write-up: problem, research, PRD, what you cut and why, launch, usage numbers and what you learned.

nodes.title: Interview preparation and job search
nodes.summary: Look for Associate PM (APM) programmes and analyst roles. Practise product-sense questions (improve or design a product), metrics questions and behavioural answers using STAR. Many people move into PM after starting as engineers or analysts.

resources.title: A day with Atlassian's Associate Product Managers
How to think like a Product Manager – Inside Atlassian

nodes.proof: Do 5 mock interviews (2 product-sense, 2 metrics, 1 behavioural) with a peer and note what to improve.

sources.title: A day with Atlassian's Associate Product Managers
